items.note: Controlled cross-cultural experiment in which Indian and US participants complete culturally grounded writing tasks with and without GPT-4o suggestions; outcomes are writing style homogenization toward Western norms and efficiency; assignment method not stated in the abstract (within-person order randomization to be checked); same study as arXiv 2409.11360.
Systematic review and taxonomy of how human-AI co-creativity studies measure creativity; it synthesizes measurement methods, not effects, so it may give no pooled numbers.
Topic-modelling systematic mapping review of 61 publications (2023 to June 2025) on generative AI and creativity; a mapping exercise with no pooled effect estimates.
Compares AUT originality and RAT scores of 46 human participants with ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemini 2.0; no participant receives AI help.

Framework that compares the diversity of model-only generations from three LLMs with matched unaided human baselines (stories, slogans, AUT) without human-AI interaction data; borderline model_only, since the human baselines may be existing datasets; abstract from the arXiv abstract page (API returned empty).

Randomised crossover in which design-engineering undergraduates alternate between ChatGPT-assisted and unaided ideation (728 ideas), scoring fluency, flexibility, originality, thematic homogenization, and semantic divergence; number of students not in the abstract and must be checked against the 50-person threshold.

52 participant pairs (104 people) do the Alternate Uses Test with or without ChatGPT-4, followed by an unaided post-test (relevant to after_ai); assignment method not stated; pairs may be the unit of analysis.

Mixed-methods paper: a qualitative study plus a quantitative study linking autonomy frustration and editing of AI advice to objective creative performance; the abstract does not say whether any condition varies AI assistance, so it may be correlational within an AI condition (likely out at full text); SSRN version W4410156412.

78 fifth-graders randomly assigned to visual art instruction with AI-generated images versus classical images; paintings rated on creativity and originality among other criteria; AI is a teacher-provided material, not a tool students use, so whether it counts as AI assistance needs a check.

Large experiments with a representative US adult sample: AI-versus-human creative ideas, a HumanPlusAI arm (search notes say random assignment, optional AI use) rated against human baselines, and a competition-from-AI arm; N not in the abstract (Crossref SSRN record); IZA DP 17302.
